name: Match the system to its metric
note: For each system, pick the metric that matches how the output is actually used. Then see what the tempting wrong choices quietly hide.

systems.system: A fraud model scores every transaction; investigators work the top ~200 flagged cases a day — no more, no less.
systems.failure: Accuracy is ~99% just by calling everything legitimate. AUC grades the entire ranking, but investigators only ever see the top k — so the number that matches the real workload is the precision of those top k cases.
systems.why: The metric has to mirror how the output is used: a fixed-capacity review queue, not the whole ranked list.

systems.system: A model outputs the probability a policy files a claim, and that probability is multiplied into the premium customers pay.
systems.failure: A model can rank risk almost perfectly (AUC 0.95) and still be badly miscalibrated — saying 5% when the true rate is 20%. When the probability itself is the product, a ranking metric can look great while the prices are wrong.
systems.why: When the calibrated probability is the deliverable, you must evaluate the probability, not just the ordering.

systems.system: A retrieval-augmented assistant answers from retrieved documents; some answers add confident facts the documents never stated.
systems.failure: A fluent answer can match a reference yet be unfaithful to the retrieved context (unsupported additions), or be faithful but built on the wrong context. A single overall score hides which failure is happening — and the two have opposite fixes.
systems.why: Generation-with-sources needs a metric that separates 'is it grounded?' from 'is it grounded in the right thing?'.
